species_affected.value: chickens and turkeys mainly; also ducklings, pigeons, canaries, geese and other wild or pet birds
also reported in pet parrots, ducks (especially mallards), captive falcons and hawks, and the wild kakapo parrot

pathogen.value: Aspergillus fumigatus most commonly, also A. flavus and A. niger; other molds like Rhizopus, Mucor and Penicillium can cause a similar disease

how_it_spreads.value: birds breathe in fungal spores from moldy bedding, litter, feed, or dusty range areas
spores become airborne when wet, moldy bedding dries out and is then disturbed
contaminated hatchery air-handling or ventilation systems can be a recurring source
chicks can be exposed to spores while hatching from contaminated eggs or contaminated bedding

key_symptoms.value: increased mortality, especially in young birds
occasionally head tilt and tremors if the infection reaches the brain
occasionally eye plaques with mycotic keratitis

mortality.value: can be high in chicks and young poults that inhale large numbers of spores; survivors are often smaller than normal afterward

diagnosis.value: based on clinical signs and typical lesions (whitish nodules/plaques in the lungs and air sacs), confirmed with fungal culture or microscopic examination of tissue

prevention.value: do not use moldy bedding, litter or feed
avoid letting bedding get wet and then dry out, since this triggers mold growth and later releases spores when disturbed
keep ventilation good, unless the ventilation system itself is the source of contamination
do not set cracked or heavily soiled eggs for incubation
thoroughly clean and disinfect hatcheries and housing between flocks, including fungicidal disinfectants on contaminated surfaces when no birds or eggs are present

treatment_overview.value: there is no effective treatment for aspergillosis in poultry; birds can sometimes recover on their own once removed from the moldy environment

when_to_call_vet.value: Call a vet if birds show labored breathing, poor growth, or unusual die-off, since aspergillosis needs lab confirmation to tell it apart from other respiratory diseases and there is no home treatment for it.

summary.value: Aspergillosis, also called brooder pneumonia, is a fungal lung infection of young chickens and turkeys caused by breathing in mold spores from damp, moldy bedding, litter or feed. It is not spread bird-to-bird, has no effective treatment once a bird is sick, and is best managed by preventing mold in housing and removing affected birds from the contaminated environment.
